chapters.title: Myth 1: “Jesus was not a real person. He was a mythical figure created by Christians.”
Myth 2: “The Christian faith is just a repackaging of pagan myths.”
Myth 3: “Christians borrowed Christmas and Easter from pagans.”
Myth 4: “Catholic beliefs about the Blessed Virgin Mary are derived from pagan sources.”
Myth 5: “Shortly after Christ founded the Church, it underwent an apostasy, becoming the corrupt Catholic Church. The true Christian Faith went underground until the Protestant Reformation.”
Myth 6: “The Catholic Church caused the fall of the Roman Empire.”
Myth 7: “The Catholic Church suppressed certain books of the Bible (for instance, the gnostic Gospels) to control Jesus’ message.”
Myth 8: “Emperor Constantine made Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire, thus institutionalizing the Catholic perversion of the true biblical faith.”
Myth 9: “The early Christians believed Jesus was just a prophet, and not divine. The Catholic Church at the Council of Nicaea in 325 altered that belief by declaring Jesus to be God.”
Myth 10: “The collapse of Rome ushered in the Dark Ages of ignorance and misery.”
Myth 11: “After the fall of Rome, the Church persecuted pagans and practiced conversion by the sword.”
Myth 12: “The Church began mandating clerical celibacy during the Middle Ages so that it could acquire the clergy’s family property.”
Myth 13: “Medieval churches kept bibles chained up to prevent people from reading Scripture for themselves.”
Myth 14: “The Church called the Crusades to slaughter Muslims.”
Myth 16: “Medieval Islamic culture was far superior to that of Catholic Europe.”
Myth 17: “The Crusades are the reason for modern Islamic hostility toward the West.”
Myth 18: “The Church created the Inquisition to enforce absolute conformity in religious belief throughout Europe.”
Myth 19: “The Inquisition frequently used sadistic torture methods, and killed millions of people.”
Myth 20: “The Inquisition controlled the minds of Catholics by creating an Index of Forbidden Books.”
Myth 21: “The Inquisition initiated the great witch hunts in Europe and the New World, leading to millions of innocent women being burned at the stake.”
Myth 22: “The Renaissance witnessed a revival of classical arts and culture, which the medieval Church had long suppressed.”
Myth 23: “The Church forcibly castrated boys to preserve their high voices for singing in church choirs.”
Myth 24: “The Church is opposed to science, and persecuted Galileo for teaching that the earth revolves around the sun.”
Myth 25: “The Church sold indulgences and ecclesiastical offices. These abuses led to the Protestant Reformation.”
Myth 26: “Corruption in the Church was so bad that only something radical like the Reformation could fix it.”
Myth 27: “Luther and other Reformers were the first to translate Scripture into vernacular languages, which the Church had previously forbidden.”
Myth 28: “The Reformers were holy men who struggled heroically to free the true Christian faith from the superstitions of Rome.”
Myth 29: “After freeing Europe from the clutches of the Catholic Church, the Protestant Reformation inaugurated an era of peace and prosperity.”
Myth 30: “Queen Elizabeth I of England ushered in a new golden age for her people, who greeted the new Church of England enthusiastically.”
Myth 31: “In the twentieth century, the Church was the willing tool of fascists.”
Myth 32: “Pope Pius XII did nothing to help the Jews during World War II.”
Myth 33: “After World War II, the Church helped fugitive Nazis escape justice.”
Myth 34: “The Church prohibits birth control to control women’s lives, and to increase the number of Catholics.”
Myth 35: “The Church seeks to impose its teachings on democratic societies by telling its members how to vote.”
Myth 36: “There was once a female pope named Joan.”
Myth 37: “The history of the papacy is rife with greedy, lustful, worldly, and incompetent popes.”
Myth 38: “Throughout the Church’s history, popes have been concerned mainly with acquiring wealth and political power.”
Myth 39: “The pope is the Antichrist, and the Church is the Whore of Babylon.”
Myth 40: “The early Church did not recognize the primacy of the papacy.”
Myth 41: “The Church sent missionaries around the world in search of gold and land for European kings.”
Myth 42: “Catholic missionaries mistreated, enslaved, and forcibly converted native peoples in the New World.”
Myth 43: “Catholic missionaries worked as spies for foreign governments, and were rightly punished and executed for it.”
Myth 44: “Christopher Columbus was an agent of Western imperialism, cultural destruction, and genocide.”
Myth 45: “The Church is one of the wealthiest organizations in the world.”
Myth 46: “The Catholic Church is responsible for more wars than anything else in history.”
Myth 47: “Sexual abuse is a pervasive problem among Catholic clergy, probably because of mandatory celibacy.”
Myth 48: “The Church is, and always has been, an oppressor of women.”
Myth 49: “Shadowy organizations such as the Knights Templar and Opus Dei have at various times secretly controlled the Church.”
Myth 50: “The Church has a long and ugly history of anti-Semitism.”
Myth 51: “The Church used to approve of or at least tolerate slavery.”
Myth 52: “The Church’s teaching on homosexuality has changed, since there used to be a Catholic marriage rite for same-sex couples.”
Myth 53: “Marie Antoinette was a selfish and decadent Catholic queen who callously told her starving subjects to ‘eat cake.’”
Myth 54: “The alleged ‘Miracle of the Sun’ at Fátima, Portugal, in 1917, was actually a mass delusion.”
Myth 55: “Catholic historians cannot be trusted because their faith compromises their objectivity.”
